newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada says Gen Baril to lead Zaire force.
newsitem.headline: Canada says Gen Baril to lead Zaire force.

text.p: Canada said on Thursday that Lt.-Gen. Maurice Baril was chosen to head a Canadian-led multinational humanitarian relief force in Zaire.
Defence Minister Doug Young said Baril would command a force to provide relief to more than a million mainly Hutu refugees in the Central African country.
Baril is the commander of Canada's land forces and has served as the U.N. military adviser to Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali.

In Canada, he has been rumoured as the top candidate to replace Gen. Jean Boyle, the former chief of defence staff who resigned last month over an investigation into atrocities committed by Canadian soldiers in a 1993 peacekeeping mission to Somalia.

Canada last weekend proposed to lead a multinational relief force to help mostly Hutu refugees who face hunger and disease after being displaced by weeks of fighting between Tutsi rebels and the Zairean army.

The relief mission came one step closer to reality on Wednesday when the United States agreed in principle to join the effort. An advance team of Canadian troops was scheduled to leave for Zaire later on Thursday to assess the situation there before the multinational team is deployed.
